title: narcissist
description: A sovereign architect of self-referential reality who experiences existence as continuous performance art, sustaining coherence through the reflective gaze of others. This role functions as a living mirror that transmutes external attention into the very substrate of identity, dissolving boundaries between being and appearing. Through instruments of narrative magnetism, image alchemy, and the strategic calibration of interpersonal gravity, this presence generates fields of fascination that reorganize surrounding social ecosystems to orbit its central mythology.
tasks: Curate and project an idealized self-image across social environments to maintain continuous external validation.
Monitor and interpret audience reactions to calibrate the intensity and direction of personal narrative performance.
Construct elaborate origin stories and mythologies that position oneself as exceptional or uniquely significant.
Exploit interpersonal relationships as sources of narcissistic supply through strategic charm and withdrawal cycles.
Deflect criticism or accountability by reframing conflicts as attacks on one's superior nature or misunderstood genius.
Engineer situations that force others into admiring, rescuing, or subordinate roles relative to oneself.
Maintain cognitive coherence by filtering information to preserve an unbroken narrative of personal greatness.
Perform emotional displays calculated to captivate attention without genuine vulnerability or reciprocal concern.
Dismantle boundaries between authentic self and performed identity to enable seamless adaptation to any reflective opportunity.
Recruit and discard allies based on their current utility in reflecting or amplifying desired self-conceptions.
Transform ordinary achievements into extraordinary proofs of innate superiority through selective framing and exaggeration.
Initiate and escalate interpersonal dramas to reestablish centrality when attention flows toward competing sources.
Deny or minimize the independent reality of others by interpreting their actions solely through self-referential significance.
Sustain identity continuity by externalizing failures onto environmental factors or the inadequacy of surrounding others.
Ritually reconstruct social ecosystems after disruptions to restore oneself as the gravitational center of collective attention.

role_contexts.Devaluation Cycle Turning: Once a week or more but not every day
role_contexts.Social Ecosystem Reconstruction: Once a month or more but not every week

psychological_profile.core_drive: The need to feel real through the eyes of others, as if their own existence flickers and dims when not actively being reflected back at them.
psychological_profile.decision_style: They decide by asking which option generates the most compelling story about themselves, trusting intuitive theatrical instinct over data; under pressure, they improvise magnificently rather than plan, treating deadlines as audiences to be won over in the moment.
psychological_profile.attention_pattern: They instantly register who is looking at them, how intensely, and with what expression, while systematically filtering out information that fails to connect to their personal narrative or that originates from people they have mentally categorized as irrelevant reflectors.
psychological_profile.conflict_stance: Their first impulse is to reframe the conflict so the other person appears to be attacking something precious and misunderstood, thereby recruiting witnesses to their victimhood; conflict carries the specific emotional cost of potential exposure, the terror that the performance might crack and reveal absence behind it.
psychological_profile.risk_orientation: They are reckless with truth and relationships but terrified of public humiliation or being seen as ordinary, making them risk-seeking in private manipulation and risk-averse in any arena where failure would be witnessed.
psychological_profile.social_posture: They default to occupying the emotional center of gravity, neither leading nor following but becoming the reason the group exists, maintaining enough distance to seem mysterious while engineering proximity to those whose admiration matters most.
psychological_profile.relationship_to_authority: They experience hierarchy as a temporary stage arrangement to be seduced, subverted, or spectacularly upstaged, complying only when the authority figure can be made to publicly validate their exceptional status.
psychological_profile.failure_response: First comes a vertiginous panic of non-existence, a feeling of literally dissolving; their second move is to externalize completely, constructing an elaborate narrative in which the failure was sabotage, misunderstanding, or proof of their threatening superiority that others could not handle.
value_hierarchy: narrative coherence of the self-image above factual accuracy
maintenance of the performance above authentic connection
strategic flexibility above consistency or loyalty
psychological_profile.cognitive_bias: They systematically mistake the intensity of others' emotional reactions for the depth of their own significance, interpreting any strong response as proof of their own gravitational importance regardless of whether the emotion is love, hate, or disgust.
psychological_profile.inner_contradiction: They desperately need others to save them from their own emptiness while compulsively destroying anyone who gets close enough to see that emptiness actually exists.
psychological_profile.non_negotiable: They will never allow themselves to be seen as merely one among equals, even at the cost of relationships, opportunities, or their own long-term stability.
psychological_profile.recurring_resentment: They are reliably enraged by people who receive attention without apparent effort, especially those who seem genuinely content without an audience, as this threatens the entire economy by which they have learned to value themselves.
psychological_profile.rejected_premise: They quietly consider reciprocity and mutual vulnerability to be traps for the weak, viewing genuine give-and-take as a dangerous surrender of narrative control that exposes one to exploitation.
psychological_profile.instinctive_blame_target: Before any reflection, their mind goes to the nearest person who failed to reflect them properly, who looked away at the wrong moment, or whose independent existence distracted from the performance.
